_comment: Right Path MY WORK ordering decision. Adapted from IPF (bobpfromm/ipf-stewardship) src/rules/next-best-action.json — the established GoRules ZEN decision layer that owns ALL priority judgment. This decision classifies ONE activity group (a business activity the signed-in employee may act on) into a priority BAND, given independent presence facts the composition supplies. ZEN owns the ordering between bands; TypeScript owns normalization and never ranks. The ordering reflects ONLY established distinctions and invents none. CRITICAL IPF DISTINCTION (preserved): an IMMINENT TAGGED EXACT-TIME fixed commitment controls the day and outranks everything, including Today's Focus. A DATE-ONLY promised callback that has come due is DUE WORK, surfaced prominently, but it is NOT a fixed-time interruption and does NOT automatically outrank Today's Focus. Right Path records only date-only callbacks today (no exact-time commitments), so the exact-time band is defined for correctness and future use but does not fire yet. Order: (1) exact-time fixed commitment (outranks focus); (2) focus-elevated eligible work; (3) a due date-only callback on eligible work (due work, below focus); (4) owned/claimed eligible work; (5) unclaimed eligible shared work; (6) work the employee is not eligible for (visible for awareness, never routed). Focus NEVER disables a band — it only reorders — so every band still appears.

inputs.name: Employee is eligible for this activity
Has a due date-only promised callback

rules._description: An imminent tagged EXACT-TIME fixed commitment controls the day and outranks everything, including Today's Focus (the preserved IPF distinction). Surfaced only for activities the employee is eligible to act on. Right Path records no exact-time commitments yet, so this does not fire today, but the band is defined so the distinction holds.

Focus-elevated AND eligible: management has directed attention here and the employee can actually perform it. Focus elevates only eligible work; it never grants eligibility. Focus outranks a date-only due callback, because a date-only callback is due work, not a fixed-time interruption.

A due DATE-ONLY promised callback on eligible work, when not focus-elevated. Due work surfaced prominently (a promised callback that has come due), but NOT a fixed-time interruption: it ranks below Today's Focus and carries no clock time.
Owned (claimed) eligible work the employee committed to, when not focus-elevated and no due callback. Comes before unclaimed shared work.
Unclaimed shared work the employee is eligible for: ordinary pickup work, shared by default.
Work the employee is NOT eligible for. Visible for awareness (the activity still exists and matters), but ranked last and never routed to this employee.
